course_description:
This course uses the exciting intersection of physiology and ecology to explain the diversity of strategies that organisms use to survive in a complex environment. You will learn about processes within and between organisms and how the environment shapes them. Processes include gas transport, water balance, sensory biology, movement, reproduction, energy and nutrient availability, and changes in species composition. From using probiotics to managing pollination services, this course will enable you to relate these processes to the world in which we live.

How will organisms adapt to climate change? What limits an organism's fitness and performance? How do diseases influence population growth? Are there trade-offs to survival and reproduction?

These, and many other big questions, are explored in the exciting intersection of physiology and ecology. Physiology gives us "how things work", and ecology gives us "who, when, and where". Together, physiology and ecology explains how organisms have evolved diverse strategies to the same environmental challenges and conditions. Strap in for an adventure as we use comparative and integrative approaches across plant, invertebrate, non-human vertebrate and human contexts to learn about all this diversity! You will be surprised at just how integrated and interconnected life is! You can expect to finish this course with a strong appreciation to why it's important to learn about our own (human) physiology and ecology as well as the major organisms that we share our planet with.

BIOL1050 is a core and prerequisite course for students declaring various extended majors, majors, and minors in the Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours), and Bachelor of Biotechnology. Expect to work with and make new friends from a range of interests and backgrounds including agricultural biotechnology, biomedical science, cell biology, ecology and conservation biology, entomology, environmental science, food science and nutrition, food technology, genetics, human anatomy, human physiology, immunology, marine biology, medical biotechnology, microbiology, molecular and microbial biotechnology, neuroscience, plant science, and zoology. There will also be students taking this course purely out of interest, as elective study.

This course is led and administered by the School of the Environment, and draws on teaching expertise from the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, School of the Environment, and School of Biomedical Sciences.

Note about incompatible courses: You can not enrol in BIOL1050 if you have already completed BIOL1030 and BIOL1040. If you have only completed BIOL1030 or BIOL1040, you may enrol in BIOL1050.

course_aims: This course introduces students to core concepts in organism form and function and how they interact with other organisms and their environment. It provides students the pre-requisite knowledge to succeed in core second-year biology courses. This requires development of content knowledge and skills relevant to:

learning_outcomes.description: Describe form, function and coordination of key physiological processes.
Compare and contrast biological strategies across varied organisms that reflect adaptation.
Identify and describe interactions within and between organisms, and the environment.
Conduct and analyse data from laboratory studies to test hypotheses.

assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
You will complete these task sets during or immediately after specific PRA or WKS. Competency-based tasks may require you to demonstrate a practical technique or measurement skill that gets assessed by your tutor during a PRA, while analytical or comprehension tasks may require you to verbally describe or provide a written response to questions, and assessed by your lecturer or tutor during or immediately after PRA or WKS.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Extensions are not available for this assessment as the task sets are marked during class by your tutor in attendance at the PRA or WKS. If you are unable to attend your timetabled PRA or WKS due to exceptional circumstances, you may attend another within the same week in order to complete your task set that you missed. If you are unable to submit, please contact Practical Coordinator Lois Eden (l.eden@uq.edu.au) to discuss exemption (noting that only the best six of nine tasks are used for calculation).
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
Students are required to submit the task sets during or immediately after the PRA or WKS for marking therefore late penalties are not applicable. Late submissions cannot be accepted. See further below if you are unable to attend.

I’m a Control Freak Gurion Ang homeostasis, active and passive transport across the cell membrane, action potential, feedback loops Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Practical 1 Gurion Ang and Head Tutors lab safety, risk management, measurement, analog vs digital, instrument uncertainty, setup experiments for future practical Learning outcomes: L04
Sense and Sensibility Brett Ferguson neurons, neurotransmitters, types of signalling, and also why plants are cool Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Bugs, Brains, and Bad Decisions Gurion Ang and Head Tutors surface area to volume ratios, action potential (again), animal and human ethics, experimental design Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Making Sense Louise Ainscough Central, peripheral, autonomic nervous systems, types of receptors, transduction, transmission, perception, reflexes Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
(Optional) Exclusive Visit to Plant Futures Facility An exclusive behind-the-scenes visit to the on-campus Plant Futures Facility (not open to public!) Learning outcomes: L02
Practical 2 Brett Ferguson, Louise Ainscough and Head Tutors Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Breath of Fresh Air Louise Ainscough & Brett Ferguson oxygen and carbon dioxide, diffusion (again), partial pressure gradients, aerobic vs anaerobic respiration, blood, surface area to volume ratios (again) Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Growing Pains Brett Ferguson and Head Tutors analysis, interpretation and extension of data collected from Practical 2, plus a story about nitrogen fixation Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Heart to Heart Louise Ainscough cardiovascular system and organs, single and double circulation, open vs closed circulatory systems, animal vs plant transport Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Practical 3 Louise Ainscough, Brett Ferguson and Head Tutors Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Water you doing? Gurion Ang conditions vs resources, water cycle, osmoregulation and osmolarity Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Huff, Puff, and Grow Louise Ainscough and Head Tutors analysis, interpretation and extension of data collected from Practical 3 Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Why are Giant Pandas Useless? Gurion Ang Food chains, nutrients and nutrient deficiency, food processing and enzymes, intracellular and extracellular digestion, digestive systems, microbial communities Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Practical 4 Gurion Ang and Head Tutors plasmolysis, osmotic stress and tolerance (plant and animal) Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Feel the Burn Louise Ainscough and Gurion Ang membrane potential (again), musculoskeletal systems, locomotion, movement and dispersal Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Making Every Drop Count Gurion Ang and Head Tutors salt and salt excretion, nitrogen and nitrogenous wastes, blood pH regulation Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Let it Grow (Dr. Seuss The Lorax version) Rebecca Dunlop Life history choices in monotremes, marsupials, mammals and the big four land plants Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Signals and Mate Competition Gurion Ang Ecological competition, biological fitness, environmental signals and recognition, intraspecies interactions Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Reproduction: Required Parts Rebecca Dunlop and Head Tutors Animal reproduction gross and fine scale anatomy Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Reproductive Strategies Gurion Ang and Elin Charles-Edwards r vs K reproduction, population ecology, population growth, interspecies interactions, human demography Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Reproduction: Pack and Send Gurion Ang and Head Tutors Pollination, functional ecology, symbiotic interactions, dispersal strategies (plant focussed) Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
